newsitem.title: USA: Plum Creek sees record year in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Plum Creek sees record year in 1996.

text.p: Plum Creek Timber Co LP said Thursday it should report record earnings in 1996 due to favorable pricing for lumber and logs and a one-time gain from asset sales.
Earlier, Plum Creek reported third quarter net income of $0.75 per unit on revenues of $173 million versus $0.60 a unit on revenues of $152 million in last year's third quarter.
"Firm demand for wood products should result in a continued favorable pricing environment for lumber and logs in the fourth quarter," the company said in a statement.

"This favorable environment, combined with the expected one-time gain from the anticipated fourth quarter closing of our previously-announced Newport asset sale, should result in record earnings for the full year 1996."
Plum Creek's previous record earnings came in 1994, when it reported net income of $112 million, or $2.36 per unit, according to a company spokeswoman.

In September, Plum Creek announced the sale of 107,000 acres of timberland in northeastern Washington and northern Idaho, as well as its Colville, Wash. sawmill, to Stimson Lumber Co for $150 million.

The company said the robust housing market in the United States contributed to its strong third quarter earnings performance. Lumber prices were up 14 percent over 1995's third quarter and eight percent from 1996's second quarter.
Plum Creek also noted prices for logs were up three percent from the second quarter due principally to the export market and stronger housing starts in Japan.
